name: Iraq
summary_text: Iraq is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely — it now has one of the world's most explicitly anti-trans statutes, in force since 1 July 2024. Amendments to the 1988 anti-prostitution law criminalise same-sex relationships (10–15 years), “biological sex change based on personal desire and inclination” (criminalising transition itself), and men who “intentionally act like women” (1–3 years) — a direct statutory criminalisation of trans feminine expression. Promoting homosexuality carries a minimum 7-year sentence. President Rashid signed the law on 29 June 2024. Behind the statute stands a documented milieu of lethal violence: militia-led campaigns against men perceived as gay or gender-nonconforming (HRW's “They Want Us Exterminated” documented mutilated bodies dumped as warnings), with impunity. Most LGBT Iraqis hide their identity entirely. The Kurdistan Region has not passed the federal law but shares the social climate and has no protections. For a visitor: being visibly trans is a statutory offence; discovery risks 1–3 years, with severe custodial and militia risk beyond the legal penalty.

sources.title: Iraq: Repeal Anti-LGBT Law | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (May 2024): 'Iraq: Repeal Anti-LGBT Law' — parliament's April 2024 amendment to the Law on Combatting Prostitution punishes same-sex relations with 10-15 years and gender-affirming care or 'imitating women' with 1-3 years; HRW urges full repeal.

sources.title: Iraq criminalises same-sex relationships in new law - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: BBC (April 2024): Iraq's parliament passed a bill criminalising same-sex relationships with 10-15 years' imprisonment; trans people face 1-3 years; also criminalised are 'promoting homosexuality', gender-reassignment surgery, men who 'intentionally' act like women, and 'wife swapping'. An earlier draft proposing capital punishment was amended after US/Western opposition.

NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Library of Congress Global Legal Monitor entry (May 2024) documents Iraq's new law prohibiting prostitution, homosexuality and gender-change procedures.

sources.title: IRAQ | LGBTIQ community under threat following law criminalizing diverse gender identities and same sex relationships — ILGA Asia
sources.claim_summary: ILGA Asia briefing note (Jan 2025): Iraq's April 2024 bill (amending the 1988 anti-prostitution law) was signed 29 June 2024 and entered into force 1 July 2024 - 'establishing a homosexual relationship' carries 10-15 years; 'promoting homosexuality' at least 7 years plus fines; gender-affirming healthcare criminalised (up to 3 years for accessing or performing); cross-dressing or men 'imitating women' up to 3 years or fines. Situation for defenders has deteriorated sharply, with fears of surveillance and crackdowns.

UK Home Office CPIN Iraq: Sexual orientation and gender identity and expression (v3.0, July 2025): assessment of risk from state and hybrid actors and non-state actors, protection, internal relocation and certification for LGBT+ asylum claims, with detailed country information.

US State Department 2012 Human Rights Report for Iraq: documents sectarian violence, torture, impunity, and 'societal discrimination and violence against individuals based on perceived sexual orientation and gender identity' - official acknowledgment of the dangers facing LGBT Iraqis.

sources.title: Prominent Iraqi TikToker fatally shot in Baghdad amid crackdown on LGBTQ community | CNN
sources.claim_summary: CNN (Sep 2023): 'Prominent Iraqi TikToker fatally shot in Baghdad amid crackdown on LGBTQ community' — a well-known young creator killed as security forces detain LGBTQ people.

sources.title: Witch-hunt in Iraq - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: BBC News investigation (Sept 2012): 'Witch-hunt in Iraq' - law enforcement agencies involved in systematic, deadly persecution of gay people; dozens if not hundreds killed since the US invasion (HRW 2009 report); only one safehouse in Baghdad housing three people; the UN said state neglect makes Iraq 'a perpetrator in the crimes'.
